person.persName: slob dpon chen po dpal mar me mdzad ye shes
paN+Di ta dI paM ka ra
ma hA paN+Di ta mar me mdzad ye shes

person.note:
See [BAQ9MH4T]: 193 for the main events of his life.
Three manuscript editions of his writings and translations were deposited respectively in rNgog Blo ldan shes rab's tomb, in the monastery of gSang phu (probably in the main assembly hall), and in Drin las kyi sde (ID:4357) ([7FZ3B926]: 107).

person.persName: zhang tshe spong chos kyi bla ma
zhang tshes spong chos kyi bla ma
tshes spong ba chos kyi bla ma
zhang tshe spong pa chos kyi bla ma
ne'u thog pa chos kyi bla ma
person.note: Third abbot of gSang phu ne'u thog monastery. Author of several commentaries, see [R894SIKE]: 405 (zhang tshe spong ba chos kyi bla mas kyang TI ka 'ga' re brtsams). Part of the group of the four main disciples of rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786) exX0032026-09-0202-25-28 .

Further holy places associated to him are: Ze thang, Grwa thang and rMog po ([647FFPZR]: 545, based on [Q3KCZX7B]: 38). Remembered for thirteen distinguished objects (such as royal insignia and religious articles), which could be objects of his clan ([4LDAV8UH]: 95.).

His dates can be approximated as 1070-1130.
He is possibly the same person as Byang 'chad khyung (ID:6382), as [NA9AMDH6] states that Khyung rin chen grags held Byang 'chad (ID:4416) and taught Sa chen (ID:4205) there ([647FFPZR]: 543). [CJ75QQKN]: 339 (fol. 8a/170a1-3). dMar ston's Zhib mo rdo rje ([RA3FK3BK]: 134 and 137), on the other hand, distinguish the two figures and places Sa chen's studies with Khyung at Nyang stod byang 'chad, and those with Khyung rin chen grags at Nyang stod.
On the reference to Khyung as "slang pa/slang pha/slang pha ba" (understood as a regionalism for "glang pa/glang pha ba," see [WL39GVT5]: 940.

The last trace of his existence is in 1144 when he took over the head of rgyal lha khang.").

person.persName: dge bshes ston pa chen po
person.note:
Celibate householder from the Byang region, chief disciple of Atiśa (ID: 3745) ([Q922IUFM]: 30).
dGe 'dun grub pa (ID:7060) is renowned as his reincarnation and his 'Brom ston-like qualities are described ([BKUHJCNA]: 787-790).

person.note: Van der Kuijp ([H9MPLMTV]) proposed the dates (?-1185). The terminus ante quem for gTsang nag pa's death was pushed to 1192 by Schwabland ([Q8WU9EDW]: 794, n. 3) on account of the date of Khro pu lo tsA ba (ID:3878)'s studies with gTsang nag pa. This date was corrected to 1195 based on Khro phu lo tsA ba's biography (van der Kuijp, personal communication).

person.persName: dan bag pa smra ba'i seng ge
smra ba'i seng ge dan 'bag pa

smra ba'i seng ge dar 'bag pa
person.note: Part of the group of Phya pa (ID:3831)'s students referred to as the "Eight Mighty Lions." Possibly identical with (ID:6217) ([4LWBNM7B]: 106). Maybe the same person as the "Chos kyi grags pa" mentioned as lineage successor of gTsang nag pa (ID:3839) and predecessor of gNyal zhig (ID:3887) in Bu ston's lineage of the Pramāṇaviniścaya (ID:3774).

person.persName: nyang bran pa chos kyi ye shes
person.note: Maybe the same person as "Nyang bran chos kyi seng ge" (ID:3844), as suggested in [CCSBSVCA]: 164, n. 416. However, A khu ching distinguishes the two. Author of manuals on the Śīkṣāsamuccaya (ID:3742) - see (ID: 6558) - and Bodhicaryāvatāra (ID: 3727). See [R894SIKE]: 405 (zhang tshe spong ba chos kyi bla mas kyang TI ka 'ga' re brtsams shing de'i slob ma nyan bran pa chos kyi ye shes kyis ni bslabs pa kun las btus pa dang | byang chub sems dpa'i spyod pa la 'jug pa la sogs pa spyod phyogs kyi yig cha dang |) and [EG6VZ8JK]: 26, translated from [8GL7ZT7Y]: 15b2 (chos kyi ye shes kyis bslab spyod sogs byang chub sems dpa’i sde sogs la bshad nyan yun ring zhing rnam bshad mang po mdzad ).

person.persName: chos grags gnyis pa gzhon nu rin chen
chos grwa gsar ma gzhon nu rin chen
person.note: Fl. late 13th to early 14th c. We assume that the gZhon nu rin chen who was abbot of gSang phu is the same person as the author of the two works by gZhon nu rin chen. The latter is characterized in [8H6M69W4], No. 15506, as the "student of Nyang" (nyang gi slob ma), which, in view of the colophon of (ID:4625), is Nyang bran pa Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) rather than Nyang bran pa Chos kyi seng ge (ID:3844).
Might be the same person as dDang phyug rin chen (2) (ID:6392).

person.note: Indian paṇḍita. Not to be confused with three Tibetan scholars with the nickname "'Bum phrag gsum pa": (ID:6415), (ID:6416), (ID:6417). See [2X2E3882]: 252, n. 130.

person.persName: zhang ye ba smon lam tshul khrims

person.note: Likely the same person as Zhang e pa (ID:6660).
Might be the same person as Tshul khrims skyabs (ID:3912).
This may be the Indic figure Kanakavarman (P5654) that was a teacher of Pa tshab nyi ma grags (ID:3868), and with whom the latter collaborated with to translate the Madhyamakāvatāra (ID:3726)
[G36YV3ZE]: 142, mentions that he was a bLa ma from Grum bu lung of gZad.

བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་བསླབ་པ་ཀུན་ལས་བཏུས་པའི་ཏི་ཀ་མདོ་སྡེ་ཉི་མའི་སྙིང་པོ

dge slong gzhon nu rin chen gyis mdzad pa'i bslab pa kun las btus pa'i Tik+ka
mdo sde kun las btus pa'i ti ka mdo'i nyi ma'i snying po
bibl.author: gzhon nu rin chen
bibl.note:
The work description in the closing verses (mdo sde kun las btus pa'i don...) and colophon (mdo sde kun las btus pa'i ti ka) indicates a commentary on the Sūtrasamuccaya (ID:3738), but in terms of its contents, the work is a commentary on the Śikṣāsamuccaya (ID:3742).
According to the colophon ex21022023-09-181, gZhon nu rin chen relies on the explanations of "Chos kyi ye shes" - this is Nyang bran Chos kyi ye shes (ID:3876) in view of the reference to "Nyang gi bran" in the conclusive verses - and that of "brTson 'grus seng ge," likely gTsang nag pa (ID:3839), as the latter was a student of Nyang bran. The author refers with name to Atiśa ("jo bo chen po", (ID:3745)), Lo tsha ba=rNgog Blo ldan shes rab (ID:3786), and Nyang bran (ID:3876), and refers anonymously to the views of other Tibetan scholars, some of whom (Zhang tshes (ID:3805), Lo tsha ba (ID:3786), sTag lo (ID:7033), Khyung (ID:3809), etc.) are identified in interlinear glosses in instance (ID:4624); the glosses are concentrated in the first 12 folios then resume at two-thirds of the text on after a long break.
The work could correspond to the "bslab btus Tik+ka" listed by A khu ching shes rab rgya mtsho in his Tho yig ([5RXEUKD9]: 514, No. 11073: gzhon nu rin chen gyi bslab btus Tik+ka).

yin te | bzod pa thostho× pa'i sngon du 'gro bar bshad pa'i phyir dang | thos pa ji ltar bya ba'i tshul yang phan yon lasogs pa'i sgo nas de ma thag tu 'chad par 'gyur ba'i phyir dang | thos pa ma byas par yang thos pa'i don bsgom pa la brtson 'grus rtsom pa mi rigs pa'i phyir ro ||

yang kha 1 stag lo don dang bcas pa'i bstan bcosbstan bcos lasogs pa thos pa byas pa la brtson 'grus rtsoM
| ste zhes bya ba'i don yin pas nyes pa med do zhes zer ba yang mi 'thad de || don dang bcas pa'i bstan bcos mnyan par bya'o zhes 'og nas 'chad pa dang zlos par 'gyur ba'i phyir ro ||

lg.l: mdo sde kun las btus pa'i don ||
kha ba can du nyang gi bran ||
chos kyi spyan gyis legs bshad pa'i ||
rjes 'brangs khyad par gzhon nus bkod ||

ab.seg:
mdomdo'/mdos? sde kun las btus pa'i ti ka mdo' nyi ma'i snying po zhes bya ba | thugs kyi me long yongs
su dag pa la byang chub kyi sems rgya chen po × snang zhing dben pa'i gnas la thugs gzhol ba mtshan nas brjod par dka' ba'i slob dpon dbang phyug rin chen zhes bya ba'i zhabs kyi rdul spyi bos blangs nas | mkhas pa'i skye bo chen po lung dang rigs pa la rtogs pa'i snang pa bsam gyis mi khyab pa dang ldan pa chos kyi ye shes zhes bya
ba dang brtson 'grus seng ge zhes bya ba'i legs par bshad pa la sgro skur gnyis dang bral bar smra ba | shag kya'i dge slong gzhon nu rin chen gyis legs par sbyar ba || || rdzogs sh+O || || bkra shis par gyur gcig ||
